why.txt: A first element said with a later इत् letter names everything from it up to that marker: अच् = the vowels, सुप् = the case endings, तिङ् = the verb endings. Look-alikes are not pratyāhāras: feminine आप् (टाप्, डाप्), a root like इण्, a suffix like अण्. (Kaumudī: “अन्त्येनेता सहित आदिर्मध्यगानां स्वस्य च संज्ञा स्यात्”)

A vowel with त् after it stands only for vowels of its own length: अत् = short अ, आत् = long आ, एत्/ओत् = two-mora ए/ओ, not pluta. Check it is a real tapara: आत् may be the 5th case of अ (आद्गुणः), and a त् may belong to the form. (Kāśikā: “तपरो वर्णस्तत्कालस्यात्मना तुल्यकालस्य … ग्राहको भवति”)

A vowel with त् after it stands only for vowels of its own length: अत् = short अ, आत् = long आ, एत्/ओत् = two-mora ए/ओ, not pluta. Check it is a real tapara: आत् may be the 5th case of अ (आद्गुणः), and a त् may belong to the form. (Kāśikā: “तपरो वर्णस्तत्कालस्यात्मना तुल्यकालस्य … ग्राहको भवति”)

paribhashas.effect: corrected by the paribhāṣā audit: effect says "only the short ओ"; ओ has no short form — तपर ओत् means the two-mora ओ (pluta excluded)

q: to what is the name given?

why.txt: a qualifier (viśeṣaṇa), agreeing with the word it qualifies (viśeṣya), stands for whatever ENDS in it — so we read “…-अन्त”; only the qualifier, never the qualified word (Nyāsa: “विशेषणेन चतदन्तविधिः [= च तदन्तविधिः], न विशेष्येण”)

A vowel with त् after it stands only for vowels of its own length: अत् = short अ, आत् = long आ, एत्/ओत् = two-mora ए/ओ, not pluta. Check it is a real tapara: आत् may be the 5th case of अ (आद्गुणः), and a त् may belong to the form. (Kāśikā: “तपरो वर्णस्तत्कालस्यात्मना तुल्यकालस्य … ग्राहको भवति”)

why.txt: the substitute stands in the 1st case — Mahābhāṣya on 1.1.57: “आदेशः प्रथमानिर्दिष्टः”

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. paribhashas.effect: named here, not applied — Vasu mentions 1.1.56 only to explain WHY some liṭ endings are pit (णल् replaces तिप् and is pit by sthānivad-bhāva → बिभेद) — an example-level derivation. The vṛtti's अपित् is carried from 1.2.4 (Kāśikā: ‘अपिदिति वर्तते’), not produced by 1.1.56; no Sanskrit commentary on 1.2.5 mentions स्थानिव at all.

quote.q: The pit terminations of the Perfect are not kit; and therefore we have बिभेद 'he has divided,' where the root is gunated before the 3rd person singular termination णल् which is a पित् termination, because it being the substitute of तिप् is regarded like तिप् by [[1.1.56]].

why.txt: a qualifier (viśeṣaṇa), agreeing with the word it qualifies (viśeṣya), stands for whatever ENDS in it — so we read “…-अन्त”; only the qualifier, never the qualified word (Nyāsa: “विशेषणेन चतदन्तविधिः [= च तदन्तविधिः], न विशेष्येण”)

why.txt: A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. why.txt: A vowel with त् after it stands only for vowels of its own length: अत् = short अ, आत् = long आ, एत्/ओत् = two-mora ए/ओ, not pluta. Check it is a real tapara: आत् may be the 5th case of अ (आद्गुणः), and a त् may belong to the form. (Kāśikā: “तपरो वर्णस्तत्कालस्यात्मना तुल्यकालस्य … ग्राहको भवति”)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

A carried option word counts only where it is still in force (the commentary may call a rule nitya). बहुलम् is wider than an option. (Kāśikā: “विभाषाधिकारेऽपि नित्यसमास एवायम्।”)

why.txt: A suffix named as a known element stands for the word from the base it was added to up to that suffix (सन् → सन्नन्त). why.txt: A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

विभाषा names ‘not’ and ‘optionally’ together, so the rule's operation is optional; वा and अन्यतरस्याम् work the same way. A carried option word counts only where it is still in force (the commentary may call a rule nitya). बहुलम् is wider than an option. (Kāśikā: “विभाषाधिकारेऽपि नित्यसमास एवायम्।”)

q: to what is the name given?

why.txt: अधि here means the word अधि itself, not its meaning or its synonyms — काशिका on 1.1.68: “शास्त्रे स्वमेव रूपं शब्दस्य ग्राह्यं बोध्यं प्रत्याय्यं भवति, न बाह्योऽर्थः”

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

विभाषा names ‘not’ and ‘optionally’ together, so the rule's operation is optional; वा and अन्यतरस्याम् work the same way. A carried option word counts only where it is still in force (the commentary may call a rule nitya). बहुलम् is wider than an option. (Kāśikā: “विभाषाधिकारेऽपि नित्यसमास एवायम्।”)

why.txt: the suffix named in the 1st case is what is introduced

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

paribhashas.effect: carried in from the sūtras named
named here, not applied — The quoted Nyāsa sentence says the opposite: '<<तस्मिन्निति निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य>> [[1.1.66]]  इति परिभाषा नोपतिष्ठते। शब्दे हि सप्तमीनिर्दिष्टे सतीयमुपतिष्ठते, नार्थे।'

quote.q: नन्वेवप्यर्थस्यैषा संज्ञा स्यादिति `खरवसनायोः`  [[8.3.15]]  इत्यत्र <<तस्मिन्निति निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य>> [[1.1.66]]  इति परिभाषा नोपतिष्ठते

paribhashas.effect: named here, not applied — The Nyāsa uses the wording of the sūtra text “उरण् रपरः” (र् not made visarga) as a jñāpaka for 1.4.110; 1.1.51 is not applied.

quote.q: तदनुपस्थाने च परेण रेफेण रेफान्तस्य रथ इत्येतस्य पदस्य पूर्वो यो रेफस्तस्य व्यवहितस्यापि विसर्जनीयः स्यात्, नैष दोषः; ज्ञापकान्न भविष्यति, यदयं <<उरण् रपरः>> [[1.1.51]]  इति व्यवहितस्य रेफस्य विसर्जनीयमकृत्वा निर्देशं करोति, तज्ज्ञापयति- व्यवहितस्य रेफस्य विसर्जनीयो न भवतीति
